conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about three children - Alex who's 7, Blake who's 20, and Charlie who's also 7.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. You're asking about three children: Alex (7), Blake (20), and Charlie (7).

Let me start by asking some questions to assess eligibility for each child.

**First, do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship and living arrangements with each child.

**Do all three children (Alex, Blake, and Charlie) currently live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, all three of them live at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to ask about Blake, who is 20 years old. 

**Is Blake currently in approved education or training?** 

(Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training, but Blake is 20, so this is important to clarify.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake isn't in any education or training. He's actually working full-time now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to ensure I have all the details needed.

**For Alex and Charlie (both age 7), are either of them currently in hospital or in care, or receiving any benefits in their own right such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither Alex nor Charlie are in hospital or in care, and they don't receive any benefits in their own right.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment.

**Are you responsible for Alex and Charlie's care - meaning you're providing for their needs such as food, clothes, and accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I provide for all their needs - food, clothes, accommodation, everything they need.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex or Charlie?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, here's my assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit:

**For Alex (age 7): ELIGIBLE ✓**
You qualify for Child Benefit for Alex as they are under 16, live with you in the UK, you're responsible for their care and providing for all their needs, and no one else is claiming for them.

**For Blake (age 20): INELIGIBLE ✗**
Unfortunately, you do not qualify for Child Benefit for Blake. Child Benefit normally only continues for young people up to age 20 if they remain in approved education or training. Since Blake is 20 years old and working full-time rather than being in education or training, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Blake.

**For Charlie (age 7): ELIGIBLE ✓**
You qualify for Child Benefit for Charlie as they are under 16, live with you in the UK, you're responsible for their care and providing for all their needs, and no one else is claiming for them.

**Summary:** You can claim Child Benefit for Alex and Charlie, but not for Blake. If you haven't already claimed, you should apply for Child Benefit for Alex and Charlie.

Please note: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.
